title: Factored claim record (per axis)
description: M0 of the factored-record migration (docs/design/VERDICT_REPRESENTATION.md §3 + VERDICT_REPRESENTATION_MIGRATION.md). Replaces the single per-axis verdict TOKEN with a factored, typed record; the legacy token survives only as a pure rendering rho(record) so determinism + the ~300 golden tests are preserved. ZERO runtime consumers at M0 — this schema + validators/validate_claim_record.py + docs/design/examples/ prove the record is coherent BEFORE any skill emits it (the M1 shadow). The record factors the four concerns a single token conflates: WHAT (finding), WHY (mechanism), FOR-WHAT (modality_scope), HOW-SURE (certainty). Cross-field invariants (open-world availability => non-committal finding; magnitude value requires a scale; finding.state in the axis enum) are enforced by the validator, not by JSON Schema alone.

axis.description: The gate / sub-skill this record governs (matches a resolver `gate:` short, e.g. 'safety', 'genomic_alteration'). For v1, finding.state is validated against this axis's resolver emitted-verdict set.

finding.description: WHAT the evidence says, factored from what-it-means-for-a-nomination (that is the gate's job, not the record's).

state.description: Closed per-axis finding token. For v1 this reuses the axis resolver's emitted verdict enum, PLUS the sentinel 'unknown' (mandatory when availability is open-world). Validator enforces membership.

direction.description: Valence toward a nomination. MUST be 'neutral' when availability is open-world (a not_wired record cannot carry a direction) — validator invariant.

magnitude.description: HOW MUCH — ordinal level binned to decision cutpoints, with the raw value + distance-to-cut retained (late, non-destructive discretization). certainty NEVER multiplies into magnitude (a strong inferred signal != a strong measured one) — they are orthogonal coordinates.

value.description: Raw measured value (e.g. log2fc, LOEUF, CERES). null when the finding is categorical / open-world. If non-null, `scale` MUST be non-null (validator invariant — no bare numbers).

scale.description: Unit / scale of `value` (e.g. 'log2fc', 'loeuf', 'ceres', 'copies_per_cell'). Required whenever `value` is non-null.

distance_to_cut.description: Signed distance of `value` from the decision cutpoint that bins `level`. Preserves near-threshold information for the borderline bin.

availability.description: The absence/presence TYPE, the axis of the ignorance-vs-negation distinction. OPEN-WORLD ignorance {not_wired,data_blocked,read_error} => ACQUIRE (and forces finding.state='unknown', direction='neutral'). MEASURED-but-underpowered {insufficient} => HOLD-WEAK. CLOSED-WORLD {measured_negative,measured_positive} => KILL/PASS. Question malformed for this target {out_of_scope} => n/a. Mirrors vocabularies/availability_state.enum.yaml, extended with the measured_* and out_of_scope closed-world states.

mechanism.description: WHY / which mechanistic class. Optional — omit on axes where mechanism is not meaningful.

classes.description: Set of MoA classes (set-union under the Fold). Drawn from the MoA ontology.

modality_scope.description: FOR WHAT modality the finding holds. 2-channel base (small_molecule vs biologics) per I5 (Phase-0b: SM-vs-biologics diverges 69%, ADC-vs-TCE only 8% — the sub-split is a refinement, not a default axis). _refinements carry per-channel divergence ONLY where a named discriminator fires (allele-selectivity, endocytosis, essential-normal-tissue, E3-substrate).

_refinements.description: Optional sub-channel divergence; each key present ONLY when a named discriminator justifies departing from its base channel.

certainty.description: HOW SURE — orthogonal to magnitude, downgrade-only. Adopted VERBATIM from the shipped CERTAINTY_MODEL.md {level, coverage, corroboration, unknown_mass} + strength, which 6 axes and validate_certainty_disjointness.py already speak. Its job is to COARSEN resolution (thin cohort => degrade to a coarser level, never a crisp pass).

level.description: min(coverage, corroboration) per CERTAINTY_MODEL.md; when corroboration is unmeasured, level = coverage.

coverage.description: Cohort / assay power behind the finding.

corroboration.description: Ordinal strength of independent, VERDICT-DISJOINT corroboration (corroborator card must not be in the axis's verdict-precedence set — disjointness invariant), matching the SHIPPED CERTAINTY_MODEL.md certainty emitted by every _strength_certainty hook: high = corroborated, low = contradicted/thin, 'unmeasured' where no disjoint corroborator exists yet (safety/tractability/differentiation).

unknown_mass.description: Fraction of decision-relevant cards that were blind / data_unavailable (open-world ignorance mass).

strength.description: Optional per-axis strength label (informational magnitude rendering), e.g. 'strong_pattern'. Distinct from finding.magnitude.level.

provenance.description: Composition-INERT audit sidecar — never gates, always carried. The record's honesty ledger.

fired_rule_ids.description: Every rule_id in the fired set that produced this record. M1 cross-check: MUST equal the resolver's actual fired set for the axis.

cards.description: Card IDs read to produce this record.

source_product_ids.description: Optional — derived/source manifest product_ids behind the cards.

versions.description: Optional — version stamps (resolver semver, catalog snapshot, etc.).

legacy_verdict.description: M2 render-equivalence anchor: the exact legacy verdict TOKEN this record renders back to (rho(record)). For a measured finding it equals finding.state (the token survives as a field — the strangler-fig invariant); for an OPEN-WORLD record (finding.state='unknown', ignorance != negation) it preserves the specific no-data token (e.g. 'data_unavailable') that the factored finding deliberately discards, so rho(record) == the pre-migration decision.json verdict byte-for-byte. Validator guard: when finding.state != 'unknown', legacy_verdict (if present) MUST equal finding.state.

context.description: OPTIONAL (2026-09-18, decision #1 L2 layer). The claim's join key — WHAT it is a claim ABOUT, at RECORD grain (the package-grain envelope.context is coarser). Additive + optional: only tumor-presence populates it this arc; every other skill omits it and stays valid. A `required` ratchet is a LATER arc. Each dimension carries an explicit scope so 'pan-X' (scope: ALL) and 'this specific X' (scope: SPECIFIC) — and, for subtype, 'not stratified at all' (NOT_STRATIFIED) — are DIFFERENT claims that join differently, the fix for the silent empty-join the indication sentinel precedent (tests/schemas/test_indication_sentinel.py) records. The SPECIFIC<->specifier-field coupling (scope: SPECIFIC requires the id field; scope: ALL/NOT_STRATIFIED forbids it) is a validator invariant, not schema, to keep this block additive.

target.description: Reused verbatim from evidence_package.schema.json context.target (symbol + hgnc_id required; ensembl/uniprot optional).

indication.description: SPECIFIC (one OncoTree code) vs ALL (pan-cancer). oncotree_code is required iff scope == SPECIFIC (validator invariant INDICATION_SCOPE_FIELD).

subtype.description: THREE states, because 'pan-subtype' (ALL) and 'the target was not stratified at all' (NOT_STRATIFIED) are different claims — the emitted corpus has subtype_fit absent in 156/504 packages (measured), which is NOT_STRATIFIED, not ALL. subgroup_ids is required iff scope == SPECIFIC (validator invariant SUBTYPE_SCOPE_FIELD).

modality.description: SPECIFIC (one channel, from the 5 active modality.enum.yaml values) vs ALL (modality-independent claim). channel is required iff scope == SPECIFIC (validator invariant MODALITY_SCOPE_FIELD).

identity.description: OPTIONAL (2026-09-18), DERIVED — never authored by hand; every field is a function of `context`, `axis`, and the run's data/version fingerprints, and the validator RECOMPUTES each rather than trusting it. Present only when `context` is (validator invariant IDENTITY_WITHOUT_CONTEXT). context_id makes records joinable/comparable; logical_key is the stable per-(context,axis) key across releases; record_revision_id changes when the data or the rules/methods behind the record change. Filed under the ROOT, not provenance, because provenance is composition-INERT (never gates) while identity DOES gate joins.

context_id.description: sha256(canonical(context))[:16], where canonical = json.dumps(context, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')). Recomputed by the validator (CONTEXT_ID_MISMATCH).

logical_key.description: '<context_id>::<axis>' — the stable identity of this (context, axis) claim across releases. Recomputed (LOGICAL_KEY_MISMATCH).

l0_digest.description: The evidence_package.governance.resolved_release_digest (sha256(sorted input_manifest_ids)[:16]) this record was computed against — the L0 component of record_revision_id, carried so the record is self-recomputable. Emission-side R6 invariant (out of scope for this standalone-record validator): l0_digest MUST equal the enclosing package's resolved_release_digest for the same run.

ruleset_version.description: The interpretation-rules file `version` in force for this axis — the ruleset component of record_revision_id.

record_revision_id.description: sha256(logical_key + '|' + l0_digest + '|' + ruleset_version + '|' + canonical(provenance.versions))[:16] — changes when the data (l0_digest), the rules (ruleset_version), or the method versions (provenance.versions) behind the record change, but NOT when only the release_pin label changes. Recomputed (RECORD_REVISION_ID_MISMATCH).
